entries.topic: Rosicrucian manifestos and their reception; Freemasonry and papal/curial condemnations 1738-2023; P2

claims.text: Fama Fraternitatis circulated in manuscript from c.1610, printed Kassel 1614; Confessio 1615; Chymical Wedding 1616; Andreae (Tübingen circle with Besold and Tobias Hess) claimed the Chymical Wedding and later called it a 'ludibrium'; brothers heal the sick without payment; movement linked to Lutheran Protestantism; organised Rosicrucian bodies later (Gold- und Rosenkreuzer reorganised 1767/1777; Golden Dawn 1887/88; AMORC 1915; Lectorium Rosicrucianum 1924)
Confessio (1615, English in Waite) condemns 'the East and the West (meaning the Pope and Mahomet)', calls the Pope Antichrist, and has 'execrate the pope'

Adam Haslmayr saw the Fama in manuscript 1610, published his Answer 1612 (reprinted in the 1614 Fama volume); shortly afterwards Archduke Maximilian III of Austria sent him to the galleys at Genoa; released 4-5 years later; no charge stated in source

Paris 1623 placards (some on the Louvre walls) inviting readers to join the Rose Cross caused panic; Gabriel Naudé answered with Instruction à la France (1623) attacking credulity; no official Church or royal action described
Grand Lodge of London and Westminster formed 24 June 1717 by four London lodges at the Goose and Gridiron; Anderson's Constitutions 1723; union as UGLE 27 December 1813

In eminenti apostolatus, Clement XII, 28 April 1738: forbade Catholic participation in Masonry under excommunication; grounds secrecy, oaths, suspicion of heresy, 'if they were not doing evil they would not have so great a hatred of the light'; noted states had moved against lodges; Dutch States General banned meetings 1735
Providas Romanorum, Benedict XIV, 18 March 1751, confirmed and quoted In eminenti; reasons: naturalism, oaths, secrecy, indifferentism, threat to church and state

Humanum genus 20 April 1884: race of man divided into 'the kingdom of God' and 'the kingdom of Satan'; partisans of evil assisted by 'that strongly organized and widespread association called the Freemasons'; aim of 'utter overthrow' of religious and political order; ratifies decrees of Clement XII, Benedict XIV, Pius VII, Leo XII, Pius VIII, Gregory XVI, Pius IX

1917 Code canon 2335: joining a Masonic sect incurs excommunication reserved to the Holy See; 1983 Code canon 1374 does not name Masonry: 'A person who joins an association which plots against the Church is to be punished with a just penalty'

CDF declaration 26 November 1983 (Ratzinger, Hamer; approved by John Paul II): 'negative judgment ... remains unchanged'; 'The faithful who enrol in Masonic associations are in a state of grave sin and may not receive Holy Communion'

DDF note dated 13 November 2023, signed by Cardinal Víctor Fernández and approved by Pope Francis, answering Bishop Julito Cortes of Dumaguete (Philippines): 'active membership in Freemasonry by a member of the faithful is prohibited' due to 'irreconcilability between Catholic doctrine and Freemasonry'; asked Philippine bishops for doctrinal and pastoral strategy

P2: Propaganda Massonica founded Turin 1877 under the Grand Orient of Italy; Gelli venerable master 1975; Grand Orient suspended the lodge 1976, a Masonic tribunal in 1981 held it had ceased to exist after a 1974 vote; list of 962 names found at Gelli's villa 17 March 1981, published 21 May 1981; Forlani government fell; Law 17 of 25 January 1982 dissolved it; Anselmi commission majority (1984) called it a secret organisation aimed at undermining democracy; Calvi a member

Fama: Father C.R. on pilgrimage taught by sages at Damcar in Arabia, travels through Egypt and Fez, returns to Germany and founds the Fraternity of the Rose Cross; members heal the sick free, wear no special clothing, meet yearly at the House of the Holy Spirit, keep the Fraternity secret for a hundred years, each chooses a successor, C.R. as seal

entries.topic: Bavarian Illuminati record and the conspiracy myth with its antisemitic graft

claims.text: Weishaupt, professor of natural and canon law at Ingolstadt; order founded night of 1 May 1776 with five men; aims freedom from 'religious prejudices', 'a state of liberty and moral equality'; grades novice/minerval; Knigge's 13 degrees; code names Spartacus, Philo; Goethe a member; bans June 1784 (unauthorised societies), March 1785 (Illuminati expressly), August 1787 (confirmed, membership punishable by death); Weishaupt lost post, lived in Gotha

Original name Bund der Perfektibilisten, Illuminatenorden from April 1778; goals: oppose superstition, obscurantism, religious influence over public life, abuses of state power; Weishaupt anti-clerical after Jesuit hostility; recruited through Masonic lodges, Knigge from 1780; membership: ~650 verifiable end 1784, Weishaupt/Hertel claimed 2,500, historians ~1,300 (NatGeo gives 2,000-3,000); Charles Theodore edicts 1784, 1785, 1787, 1790, 2 March 1785 the 'deathblow'; papers seized 1786-87 and published 1787; Morse sermon 9 May 1798; modern groups claim descent without evidence

Barruel's Memoirs (London exile, 1797-98) argued the Revolution was a conspiracy of philosophes, Freemasons and Illuminati executed by the Jacobins; Robison's Proofs of a Conspiracy 1797-98 similar; Mounier and de Maistre rejected it; historians reject 'master conspiracy' view

Simonini letter dated 1 August 1806, received by Barruel 20 August 1806, claimed Jews founded Freemasons and Illuminati to take over Europe; Barruel did not publish it, fearing violence against Jews, but circulated it; first published 1878 in Le Contemporain; considered among earliest Judeo-Masonic conspiracy texts, believed to have inspired parts of the Protocols; Barruel burned a manuscript incorporating Jews before his death 1820

Per Danny Keren, Barruel's Memoirs did not blame Jews; the Simonini letter was fabricated, probably sent by state police; Protocols claim Jews infiltrated Freemasonry; Juan Tusquets (Catholic priest) built a Judeo-Masonic-Communist theory justifying Francoism; Le Pèlerin 1902 drawing 'Catholic France driven by Jews and Freemasons'; Nazi 1935 poster; New World Order/Bilderberg theories reuse tropes, blaming Rothschilds or 'international bankers'

Taxil: feigned conversion after Humanum genus 1884; Le Diable au XIXe siècle (1892) alleged Luciferian Palladism led by Albert Pike; Diana Vaughan; confessed hoax 19 April 1897 at the Société de Géographie, Paris; Bishop Fava and others had insisted Vaughan was real

Pat Robertson, The New World Order (1991), linked Illuminati, Freemasons, CFR, Trilateral Commission; critics (Radner, Christian Century; Michael Lind, NYRB 1995) found reliance on Nesta Webster and Eustace Mullins; ADL asked him to denounce the Jewish-conspiracy idea; Robertson said in 1995 he intended no antisemitism
Simonini signed as Jean-Baptiste Simonini 'from Florence', claimed to have posed in Piedmont as a baptised Jew wishing to reconnect with his 'nation' (audit)

Judeo-Masonic article: the fabricated Simonini letter was 'probably sent to him by members of the state police' opposed to Napoleon's liberal policy toward the Jews; 1935 German poster: Freemasonry 'beholden to Jewry' (audit)
Robertson 1995 to the NYT: regretted that anyone in the Jewish community believed his description of international bankers and use of 'European bankers' referred to Jews (audit)

entries.topic: Witch trials: bull, Malleus, courts, numbers, myths

claims.text: Summis desiderantes, Innocent VIII, 5 December 1484: names Dominican inquisitors Henricus Institoris and Jacobus Sprenger; Mainz, Cologne, Trier, Salzburg, Bremen; alleges people 'hinder men from begetting and women from conceiving', blight crops; authorises 'correction, imprisonment, and punishment'

Malleus: printed Speyer 1486 (some date 1487); author Heinrich Kramer; Sprenger credited only from 1519; bull gives general authority, not approval of the book; Cologne approbation argued by many historians to be forged, Mackay disagrees; Kramer's Tyrol prosecution failed, bishop called him 'senile and crazy'; Cologne clergy condemned it 1490; Behringer: Inquisition 'denied any authority to the Malleus'; Britannica: 28 editions 1486-1600; teaches women more susceptible, recommends torture and deception; used by secular courts; worst prosecutions 1560-1630

Execution estimates: Scarre & Callow 40,000; Levack 45,000; Hutton 40,000-50,000; Behringer and Roper 50,000-60,000; c.100,000 prosecuted c.1400-1775; ~80% of convicted women (75-85% of accused); men majority in Iceland, Finland, Estonia, Russia; Holy Roman Empire about half; Würzburg 1626-31 ~900 executions; Roman Inquisition (from 1542) restrained secular courts; Venetian Holy Office never convicted for maleficio; Roman Inquisition 1635 found 'scarcely one trial conducted legally'; Instructio warned against hasty convictions; Canon Episcopi scepticism backed by Paris 1398; Malleus opened by opposing it; last executions: Scotland 1727, Britain Witchcraft Act 1735, Salzburg 1750, Austria 1768 ban, Göldi 1782; southwest Germany 1561-1670: 2,527 of 3,229 executions in Catholic territories

Nine million: Voigt, Berlinische Monatsschrift 1784 (Luebke says 1783), extrapolated from ~30 Quedlinburg trials to all Europe; Behringer named it the 'Nine Million Theory'; a 'colossal error of misguided statistical extrapolation'; became influential myth in 20th-century feminism and neopaganism

Logroño auto de fe 1 November 1610: six burned, five in effigy; Salazar's 1611 tour with an Edict of Grace gathered ~2,000 confessions (1,384 children), most of 1,802 questioned retracted; Salazar: judges should not sentence 'unless the case can be proven with external and objective evidence'; August 1614 Council of Inquisition dismissed pending trials and issued stricter rules of evidence, ending witch-burning in Spain
Midwife-witch thesis is a historians' myth (Harley 1990); Malta study: 'wrong to assume that midwives were accused en masse'; Malleus depicted midwives as infant snatchers

Würzburg trials conducted under Prince-Bishop Philipp Adolf von Ehrenberg (1623-31), torture beyond the Carolina's limits; 157 executions confirmed in the city from an incomplete list, est. 219 in the city, est. ~900 across the prince-bishopric; 19-43 priests and at least 49 children under twelve executed; Emperor condemned in 1630 after a Speyer complaint; ended 1631 with Swedish occupation and Ehrenberg's death (16 July 1631)
Spanish Inquisition established 1478 by Ferdinand and Isabella under the control of the Spanish Crown, not directly of the papacy (audit)

Witch trials article: 'Roughly 80% of those convicted were women, most of them over the age of 40'; SW Germany 1561-1670: 702 executed in Protestant, 2,527 in Catholic territories; regional variation debated: a 2017 Economic Journal study links intensity to Catholic-Protestant religious-market contestation, French decline tied to stronger central government; Paris 1398 decree 'seemed' still to support Canon Episcopi (audit)
Würzburg: relatives' complaints against the prince-bishop reached his superiors, the Pope and the Emperor; Ernst von Ehrenberg, the bishop's nephew, executed (audit)

entries.topic: Alchemy, astrology, divination, tarot, the Index, Catechism today

claims.text: Spondent quas non exhibent, John XXII, c.1317, a decretal (Extravagantes) against fraudulent alchemists and those who coined their false metal; fine equal to weight of real gold/silver; clerics lose benefices permanently; rationale moral (fraud), alchemy not declared heretical
About a million words in Newton's alchemical manuscripts; Chymistry of Isaac Newton project, Indiana University

Tridentine Rule IX (1564): books on geomancy, hydromancy, aeromancy, pyromancy, oneiromancy, chiromancy, necromancy, sortilege, poisons, augury, sorcery, magic arts 'absolutely repudiated'; judicial astrology books claiming certainty about future events or human acts not to be read; natural observations for navigation, agriculture, medicine allowed
Sixtus V's bull Coeli et terrae (1586) endorsed the Thomist approach of the 1564 Index and prohibited 'uncertain predictions about future human actions'; Bellarmine commented

Morandi predicted Urban VIII's death for 1630, was jailed and died in prison; the next year Urban decreed death for predicting the life or death of the pope or relatives to the third degree; 1559 Index banned astrological divinations of future contingents

Tarot: trionfi added to packs in Milan/Ferrara c.1440-50 for games; Dominican sermon c.1450-70 condemned dice, cards and triumphs; divinatory use from 1780s (Dummett); Court de Gébelin Monde primitif vol. VIII 1781 Egyptian claim unsupported; Comte de Mellet essay first linked to cartomancy; Etteilla method 1783, treatise 1785, society 1788; Lévi 1861; Golden Dawn 1888; Rider-Waite-Smith 1909 (Pamela Colman Smith)

CCC 2116: 'All forms of divination are to be rejected'; consulting horoscopes, astrology, palm reading, omens, lots, clairvoyance and mediums 'contradict the honor, respect, and loving fear that we owe to God alone'; 2117 magic and sorcery 'gravely contrary to the virtue of religion', wearing charms reprehensible, spiritism warned against
